transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Lee (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (LumenHealth), Aisha Carter (LumenHealth), Tom Walters (LumenHealth)

Auto-summary (auto-section, may be rough):
- Internal enablement / onboarding for LumenHealth champions and PMs. Focus on storycrafting — tying Redwood value props to LumenHealth use cases (clinical summarization, triage routing).
- Quick demo walkthrough of two flows: low-latency triage and batch summarization, highlight Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.
- Discuss security questions (SAML + KMS) and pilot success metrics.
- Agree next steps: deliver one-pager, benchmark runbook, schedule pilot kickoff.

Topics covered: Storycrafting, champion enablement, demo flows, Dedicated vs Hosted, security (SAML/KMS), pilot metrics, pricing hints.

00:00 Maya Patel: okay uh welcome everyone thanks for joining on a Friday afternoon, um quick objective for today is to get LumenHealth champions comfortable with the narrative and a crisp demo flow they can show internally, and to surface any blockers for pilot.
00:27 Rajiv Menon: yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. we'll have about an hour. real quick i have Tom and Aisha here so we want to make sure the narrative lands for ops and product.
00:42 Connor Lee: awesome, i'll take a couple of slides then jump into the demo — there's a short run of triage flow and a batch summarization job, plus we'll touch on routing and cost controls.
00:58 Aisha Carter: quick ask — can we start with the success criteria? Tom's gonna want numbers.
01:12 Tom Walters: yeah ideally reduce triage time by 40% and keep latency under 600ms for the interactive triage UI. those are ballparks.
01:30 Maya Patel: noted, okay success criteria — triage latency <600ms, 40% task reduction, accuracy benchmark we'll define. i'll capture those.
01:48 Connor Lee: starting deck, open with problem statement — high volume of incoming clinical notes, need to prioritize and summarize for care teams. our angle: predictable inference, cost controls, private deployments when needed.
02:10 Rajiv Menon: i like the predictability bit. question: hosting — we have HIPA-ish concerns so private deployment is likely. can you outline the tradeoffs quickly?
02:26 Connor Lee: sure — hosted gives fastest time-to-value and easiest upgrades. Dedicated/reserved is predictable throughput with isolation. Private/VPC or on-prem gives you full network control and KMS/HSM options for keys. the tradeoff is ops footprint and upgrade cadence.
02:45 Aisha Carter: and what about quantization — do we lose clinical precision?
03:00 Connor Lee: good question. generally 4-bit/8-bit quantization has minimal impact on many summarization tasks but we always recommend a quick eval set. we can run a quality sweep on your prompt set as part of the pilot.
03:18 Maya Patel: quick storycraft note — when you talk to product leadership, start with the business metric (reduce clinician time) then move to the technical promise (latency, cost controls). don't lead with model architecture.
03:34 Tom Walters: that's helpful. show me how we'd pitch this in a 5 minute exec readout.
03:48 Maya Patel: script idea: 1) problem: clinicians overwhelmed, 2) solution: Redwood inference platform automates summarization and smart triage, 3) impact: X minutes saved per clinician, Y cost delta vs running own infra, 4) ask: pilot to validate on N days.
04:10 Rajiv Menon: can you include a simple TCO slide? Tom likes numbers.
04:22 Connor Lee: yeah we'll draft a rough TCO for the pilot. note — estimates depend on model choice, batch sizes, and whether you use Dedicated. we'll surface ranges.
04:38 Maya Patel: demo time — Connor, over to you.
04:45 Connor Lee: pulling up the demo app — apologies if audio is busted, i'm screen-sharing now. basic triage pipeline: ingestion -> embedding index -> triage model call -> ranked actions.
05:10 00:05:10 Connor Lee: (demo) sending a sample clinical note, showing prompt template, using a lower-context model for latency path then fallback to a higher-quality model for complex cases.
05:40 Aisha Carter: quick interruption — what's the fallback latency?
05:50 Connor Lee: typical fallback adds 200-300ms. we use prefix caching for repeated patient prefixes which reduces cold-call time.
06:10 Tom Walters: when you say prefix caching, is that per-tenant?
06:20 Connor Lee: yes you can scope caching by tenant or route, you can also control TTLs. importantly, caching is safe for idempotent prompts; sensitive content paths can skip caching.
06:42 Maya Patel: good talking point: caching reduces unit cost for repetitive workflows like post-discharge notes.
06:58 Rajiv Menon: security questions — SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs, KMS. can you confirm Redwood supports these?
07:15 Connor Lee: yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM, detailed audit logs for inference calls are available in Dedicated/Private, and KMS integrations for key wrapping. we'll share the security whitepaper after this call.
07:40 Aisha Carter: any SOC/ISO certifications?
07:47 Connor Lee: Redwood has SOC2 in scope and we maintain continuous controls — i'll confirm exact certification names in the doc i'll send.
08:02 Maya Patel: moving to storycraft roleplay — Rajiv, you're the internal PM champion, Tom you're the CTO, Aisha you run engineering. we'll do a 3 minute champion pitch then critique.
08:20 Rajiv Menon: ok cool, i'll take it. uh start: "we can reduce clinician time on notes by automating summaries with a reliable inference platform that meets our security needs..."
08:38 Tom Walters: pause — add a concrete example up front, like 'this type of note takes 7 minutes now, we can bring that to 3-4' — anchors help.
08:52 Aisha Carter: and name an early ROI scenario — e.g., reduce night-shift backlog by 60%.
09:05 Maya Patel: good. feedback: make the ask explicit — 'we'd like to run a 4-week pilot on a sample of internal notes to validate accuracy and latency'.
09:20 Rajiv Menon: noted — i'll update the champion slide.
09:30 Connor Lee: demo continue — switching to batch summarization job flow. we'll show a scheduled job that batches notes overnight using higher throughput, lower-cost quantized models.
09:55 00:09:55 Connor Lee: (demo) starting batch run: showing throughput numbers and cost estimate in the console. note the Optimize recommendations flagged a different quant profile for best cost/quality.
10:20 Aisha Carter: are there canned Optimize suggestions or is it custom?
10:30 Connor Lee: there are default heuristics, but we tune based on your seq-length distribution and latency SLOs; recommended configs are surfaced in the console and we can export them into a runbook.
10:50 Tom Walters: what about rollout and canary testing?
11:00 Connor Lee: we support canary variants by percentage traffic or by route; automatic fallback on regressions is supported if you configure monitors. we'll demo a simple canary in the pilot.
11:22 Maya Patel: objection-handling note: when customers worry about model regressions, present the eval suite and automatic rollback as the safety net.
11:36 Rajiv Menon: CRM/Procurement question — what's typical pilot licensing?
11:45 Maya Patel: often it's a month of Dedicated or a hosted usage cap plus a support credit. we'll send a pilot proposal with a few options.
12:00 Connor Lee: switching to a deeper technical sidenote — network egress for private deployment: we can work over VPC peering or direct connect. some customers prefer air-gapped on-prem; that increases lead time.
12:25 Aisha Carter: lead time estimate?
12:30 Connor Lee: for VPC deployment usually 2-4 weeks, on-prem can be 6-12 depending on approvals.
12:45 Tom Walters: okay. let's talk about measurable pilot metrics — besides latency and accuracy, what do you want us to look at?
13:00 Maya Patel: adoption rate (percent of triaged notes accepted by clinicians), cost per 1k notes, average tokens per note, and any downstream reduction in escalations.
13:20 Rajiv Menon: can you run an initial token estimate given our sample? we'll need that for the TCO.
13:30 Connor Lee: yes we'll estimate once you share sample note length distribution. I'll add that to action items.
13:48 Maya Patel: roleplay two-minute exec pitch — Connor you'll present infra choices, i'll handle the ask.
14:02 Connor Lee: quick script for infra slide: "Choice A (Hosted) — fastest deployment, lower ops; Choice B (Dedicated) — predictable throughput, isolation; Choice C (Private) — full network control and KMS".
14:24 Tom Walters: good. I want to see the rough numbers on cost per 10k notes for each choice.
14:36 Maya Patel: we'll include a comparative table.
14:48 00:14:48 Rajiv Menon: quick interjection — competitors: we've looked at Anthropic and Vertex for other projects; how do you position?
15:02 Maya Patel: high-level rebuttal: Redwood focuses on serving and operational tooling — unified runtime with caching, routing, and built-in fallback; others might offer models but not the same production controls. Connor can add specifics.
15:18 Connor Lee: right — we emphasize predictable latency, KV cache, automatic batching and compile-time kernel selection; this often beats naive endpoints for 95th percentile latency.
15:37 Aisha Carter: any customer references in healthcare?
15:44 Maya Patel: we can share anonymized case studies; i'll attach them.
15:56 Connor Lee: now quick live Q&A — Rajiv asked about evals, we can run a quality sweep against your 200-sample prompt set.
16:12 Rajiv Menon: perfect — and include edge cases for PHI sensitivity.
16:24 Tom Walters: legal will want an audit log sample — can you produce an excerpt?
16:33 Connor Lee: yes, audit log schema is available — will share sanitized examples.
16:45 Maya Patel: let's switch back to storycrafting — Aisha, play the skeptical engineer.
16:52 Aisha Carter: sure, "how do we know the summaries won't hallucinate and cause clinical risk?"
17:04 Connor Lee: honest answer: any generative system requires guardrails — we recommend a human-in-loop for high-risk decisions, conservative prompts, extractive prompts for facts, and regression monitoring tied to eval sets. we'll propose an acceptance threshold.
17:28 Aisha Carter: and if we see regressions after rollout?
17:34 Connor Lee: automatic rollback + canary isolation; plus we keep a parallel higher-quality path for escalation.
17:44 Rajiv Menon: on SLA — what's typical for Dedicated?
17:50 Maya Patel: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets are part of Dedicated enterprise packages, we'll put details in the pilot proposal.
18:05 Connor Lee: short tangent: batching strategy — for triage we favor small continuous batches to keep latency low. for overnight summarization, large batch windows minimize cost.
18:28 Tom Walters: do you support dynamic batching per route?
18:33 Connor Lee: yes, routing rules can set batch windows per route.
18:42 Maya Patel: demo wrap-up, capture two narrative scripts: 1) Exec 5-min pitch and 2) Champion 2-min pitch. we'll circulate slide snippets.
18:58 Rajiv Menon: quick procurement note — we'll need a high-level SOW for legal and a pilot price range.
19:08 Maya Patel: we'll send SOW template and a price band.
19:20 Connor Lee: last technical note — for data residency we can pin region routes; Private deployments get you local-only processing.
19:36 Aisha Carter: that works.
19:44 Maya Patel: final roleplay: Tom you close the exec ask.
19:52 Tom Walters: short close: "We want to validate on a 4-week pilot starting early July to assess latency, accuracy, and clinician adoption; if successful, expand to 6 production routes."
20:08 Maya Patel: great, that's a clear next step.
20:18 Rajiv Menon: how soon can you send the one-pager and pilot proposal?
20:24 Maya Patel: by Tuesday 2025-07-01. Connor, benchmark runbook by Thursday.
20:32 Connor Lee: will do.
20:40 Maya Patel: any final questions?
20:45 Aisha Carter: none from me.
20:48 Tom Walters: no, thanks all.
20:52 Maya Patel: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with materials and schedule the kickoff.
